plain_summary: An SBA business development program for eligible small firms. Agencies can award contracts to these firms through SBA, sometimes without competition.
why_it_matters_here: 8(a) awards can be sole source, which can raise concentration in small cells.
official_definition: established a program that authorizes the Small Business Administration (SBA) to enter into all types of contracts with other agencies and award subcontracts for performing those contracts to firms eligible for program participation.
related_terms: set-aside, SBA, small business concern, not competed

plain_summary: The date the government signed the action. USAspending ties each obligation to this date.
why_it_matters_here: action_date sets each row's fiscal year, and flags C01 to C03 and C07 to C09 test it.
official_definition: The date the action being reported (for prime award transactions or sub-awards) was issued or signed by the Government, or a binding agreement was reached.
related_terms: fiscal year, late-reported row, transaction

plain_summary: A law in which Congress approves money for a purpose. Agencies can obligate only money that has been appropriated.
why_it_matters_here: Contract actions use appropriated money, which is why non-appropriated fund buys can be left out of FPDS.
official_definition: The process by which Congress designates and approves spending for a specific purpose (e.g., a project or program).
related_terms: obligation, lapse in appropriations, Treasury Account Symbol, contract action

plain_summary: A contract, order or agreement under which the government commits money to a recipient. One award usually has many rows, the original action plus its modifications.
why_it_matters_here: We group rows into awards with contract_award_unique_key. 4,314,940 of 68,429,519 distinct awards have rows in more than one fiscal year.
official_definition: Money the federal government has promised to pay a recipient.
related_terms: transaction, modification, unique award key, IDV

plain_summary: A USAspending download page with ready-made zip files of award transactions, one per fiscal year. New files come out each month. We use the All Agencies, Contracts, Full files from the 2026-09-06 release.
why_it_matters_here: It is our only data source. We hold 18 of its zips, FY2008 to FY2025, about 88.7 million rows.
official_definition: Download major agencies’ award transaction data for full fiscal years.
related_terms: Full file, Delta file, release date, USAspending.gov, custom award download

plain_summary: The kind of award on a row. Code A is a BPA call, B a purchase order, C a delivery order and D a definitive contract. IDV rows use idv_type_code instead.
why_it_matters_here: Award type explains the FY2008, FY2015 and FY2019 row-count jumps, which came from purchase orders, delivery orders and BPA calls.
official_definition: The type of award being entered by this transaction.
related_terms: BPA call, purchase order, delivery order, definitive contract, IDV

plain_summary: The agency that issued and manages the award.
why_it_matters_here: It is the agency part of our cell. We use it over the funding agency, which carries placeholder code 999 in FY2008 to FY2010.
official_definition: The Awarding Agency is the agency that issues and administers the award.
related_terms: funding agency, subtier agency, CGAC, cell, funding agency 999

plain_summary: The full agreed value of a contract if every option were used. For an IDV it also includes the estimated value of all orders.
why_it_matters_here: The Coins 'N Things vehicle records $15 billion here against the $10 billion obligated on its vehicle record.
official_definition: For the Award it is the mutually agreed upon total contract value including all options (if any). For IDVs the value is the mutually agreed upon total contract value including all options (if any) AND the estimated value of all potential orders.
related_terms: option, potential total value of award, IDV, US Mint rows

plain_summary: The value of a contract counting the base period and any options already exercised. On a modification it records the change in that value.
why_it_matters_here: It describes contract size. Our measure uses obligations instead.
official_definition: The contract value for the base contract and any options that have been exercised.
related_terms: option, base and all options value, current total value of award

plain_summary: A published government total, from GAO or GSA, that we compare with our own yearly total. Each one has a saved copy and a verified quote.
why_it_matters_here: A match shows we extracted and summed the data correctly. It cannot catch an error inside FPDS itself.
related_terms: benchmark figure, benchmark bound, PASS/WARN/FAIL, GAO, GSA

plain_summary: A benchmark stated as a floor, such as GAO's "more than $550 billion" for FY2018. It is checked one way only, so our total passes if it is above the floor. GAO's FY2021 figure is approximate and is treated separately.
why_it_matters_here: FY2018 to FY2020 rest on bounds, which say less than exact figures.
related_terms: benchmark, benchmark figure

plain_summary: A benchmark stated as an exact total, such as GAO's $793 billion for FY2025. GAO gives these for FY2022 to FY2025.
why_it_matters_here: Our totals are within 0.2% of GAO's figure in all four of those years.
related_terms: benchmark, benchmark bound

plain_summary: A written understanding with a vendor on terms and prices for future orders. A BOA is not itself a contract, and the orders under it are.
why_it_matters_here: One of the two $10 billion US Mint rows is a basic ordering agreement for gold bullion.
official_definition: A Basic Ordering Agreement (BOA) is a type of Indefinite Delivery Vehicle (IDV). It is not a contract; it is a written understanding between government and contractor.
related_terms: IDV, US Mint rows, delivery order

plain_summary: A standing agreement with a vendor for repeat purchases, set up like a charge account. Each purchase under it is a BPA call.
why_it_matters_here: BPA calls drove much of the FY2019 row-count jump.
official_definition: A blanket purchase agreement (BPA) is a simplified method of filling anticipated repetitive needs for supplies or services by establishing "charge accounts" with qualified sources of supply
related_terms: BPA call, IDV, Federal Supply Schedule

plain_summary: A single order placed under a BPA. It is award type A in our data.
why_it_matters_here: BPA calls rose from 192,376 in FY2018 to 796,679 in FY2019, part of the FY2019 row-count jump.
official_definition: Enter this code for an award that is a call against a BPA.
pinpoint: FPDS Data Dictionary V1.5, element Award Type, value A, p. 146 (PDF p. 148)
related_terms: BPA, award type, row-count jump

also_called: Commercial and Government Entity code, cage_code, NCAGE
plain_summary: A code that the Defense Logistics Agency assigns to a company location. One company can have many CAGE codes.
why_it_matters_here: cage_code marks a vendor location, so we do not use it to define vendors.
official_definition: An identifier assigned to entities located in the United States or its outlying areas by the Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) Commercial and Government Entity (CAGE) Branch to identify a commercial or government entity by unique location
pinpoint: FAR 2.101(b), definition of CAGE code, paragraph (1)
related_terms: UEI, SAM.gov

also_called: market cell, agency x PSC x fiscal year
plain_summary: One market in our measure, meaning one awarding agency code, one PSC and one fiscal year. A blank PSC counts as its own value.
why_it_matters_here: HHI and CR4 are computed once per cell. There are 365,402 cells across FY2008 to FY2025.
related_terms: vendor-cell, market definition, awarding agency, PSC, fiscal year

also_called: 24 CFO Act agencies, Chief Financial Officers Act agencies
plain_summary: The 24 large agencies listed in the Chief Financial Officers Act of 1990, such as Defense, Veterans Affairs and GSA. Many audits and OMB rules cover only these 24.
why_it_matters_here: Many government data-quality reviews test only these 24 agencies, so their findings say little about the smaller agencies in our data.
official_definition: The CFO Act, among other things, established Chief Financial Officer positions at major federal entities. The current list of 24 included entities is commonly referred to as the CFO Act agencies.
related_terms: Senior Accountable Official, data quality certification, GAO, inspector general

also_called: CGAC agency code, toptier agency code
plain_summary: The 3-character agency code Treasury uses in account codes, such as 097 for Defense. Most awarding agency codes in our data are CGAC codes.
why_it_matters_here: It is the agency part of our cell. We keep it as text because most codes have a leading zero.
related_terms: FREC, awarding agency, funding agency, Treasury Account Symbol

also_called: Council of the Inspectors General on Integrity and Efficiency
plain_summary: The council of all federal inspectors general. It coordinates their work across agencies.
why_it_matters_here: CIGIE set the common guide and timing for the IG DATA Act audits, so their results follow one method (GAO-20-540).
official_definition: The Council of the Inspectors General on Integrity and Efficiency (CIGIE) is an independent entity established within the executive branch to address integrity, economy and effectiveness issues that transcend individual Government agencies
pinpoint: IGnet home page, What is CIGIE
related_terms: inspector general, GAO

plain_summary: Goods or services of a kind sold to the public, bought under the simpler rules in FAR Part 12.
why_it_matters_here: Cells of commercial buys may call for a different reading of concentration than cells of custom defense work.
official_definition: A product, other than real property, that is of a type customarily used by the general public or by nongovernmental entities for purposes other than governmental purposes
pinpoint: FAR 2.101(b), definition of commercial product, paragraph (1)
related_terms: FAR, PSC

plain_summary: Dollar amounts adjusted for inflation to the prices of one base year, so years compare fairly.
why_it_matters_here: HHI and CR4 use shares within one cell and year, so inflation cancels out. Dollar trends across FY2008 to FY2025 need constant dollars.
official_definition: A dollar value adjusted to remove the effects of inflation by dividing the nominal value (also called the current dollar value) by the appropriate price index.
related_terms: nominal dollars, benchmark

plain_summary: Any action that buys, rents or leases goods, services or construction with appropriated money above the micro-purchase threshold, plus any change to such an action. Grants and other transaction agreements are not contract actions.
why_it_matters_here: FPDS must hold every contract action, so this definition marks the edge of our data.
official_definition: Contract action means any oral or written action that results in the purchase, rent, or lease of supplies or equipment, services, or construction using appropriated dollars over the micro-purchase threshold
related_terms: contract action report, micro-purchase threshold, other transaction agreement, FPDS, appropriation

plain_summary: The FPDS record for one contract action. Each transaction row in our data comes from one CAR.
why_it_matters_here: Contracting officers must complete a CAR within three business days of award, so most rows are timely. DoD rows publish later.
official_definition: contract action data required to be entered into the Federal Procurement Data System (FPDS).
pinpoint: FAR 4.601, definition of contract action report
related_terms: contract action, FPDS, transaction, DoD 90-day delay

plain_summary: The specific office that awards and manages a contract.
why_it_matters_here: awarding_office_code is the finest level of buyer in our data. The cell stops at the agency level.
official_definition: Contracting office means an office that awards or executes a contract for supplies or services and performs postaward functions not assigned to a contract administration office
related_terms: subtier agency, awarding agency, contracting officer

plain_summary: The government official with legal authority to sign, manage and end contracts. The contracting officer enters each contract action in FPDS.
why_it_matters_here: Field accuracy in our data rests on what contracting officers enter.
official_definition: Contracting officer means a person with the authority to enter into, administer, and/or terminate contracts and make related determinations and findings.
related_terms: contract action report, FPDS, contracting office

plain_summary: For a contract, the total obligated so far, including the base and exercised options.
why_it_matters_here: It is an award-level running total. Summing it across rows would double count.
official_definition: For procurement, the total amount obligated to date on a contract, including the base and exercised options.
related_terms: base and exercised options value, total dollars obligated

plain_summary: A USAspending download built on request for the dates and filters you choose. It holds the same 297 columns as the archive.
why_it_matters_here: Our one-quarter test found the archive complete against a custom download. 89% of matched rows were identical in every column.
official_definition: The Assistance_PrimeTransactions and Contracts_PrimeTransactions files are generated on demand based on selected specifications.
pinpoint: Analyst's Guide, How to access the data, p. 9 (PDF p. 9)
related_terms: Award Data Archive, release date

also_called: DATA Act Information Model Schema, GSDM, Governmentwide Spending Data Model
plain_summary: The rulebook for federal spending data. It lists each data element with its definition and format, plus the validation rules. Treasury renamed it GSDM.
why_it_matters_here: Many column definitions in our files follow this model, so it is the place to check what a field was meant to hold.
official_definition: The Governmentwide Spending Data Model (GSDM) is the authoritative source for the terms, definitions, formats, and structures for hundreds of distinct data elements that tell the story of how federal dollars are spent.
related_terms: DATA Act, DATA Act Broker, USAspending.gov

also_called: Digital Accountability and Transparency Act of 2014, Pub. L. 113-101
plain_summary: A 2014 law that expanded FFATA. It made OMB and Treasury set common data standards for spending data. It also made agencies link their accounting data to their awards.
why_it_matters_here: It created the quarterly reporting, SAO sign-offs and audits behind most government reviews of the data we use.
official_definition: Expands FFATA by requiring the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) and the Department of the Treasury to develop government-wide data standards and data elements for agencies to use when reporting federal spending and requires agencies to link financial information (e.g., obligations) to the related federal awards.
pinpoint: Table 1, Laws and Regulations with Relevant USAspending.gov Reporting Requirements (PDF p. 2, no printed page number)
related_terms: FFATA, DAIMS, DATA Act Broker, Senior Accountable Official, File C, USAspending.gov, OMB

plain_summary: Treasury's system that takes in agency submissions, runs validation checks and assembles the data shown on USAspending. It also pulls award data from government-wide systems such as FPDS.
why_it_matters_here: The Broker builds File D1 from FPDS, the data behind our archive files.
official_definition: DATA Act Broker—a system that collects and validates agency data—which operationalizes the reporting framework laid out in the schema.
related_terms: DATA Act, DAIMS, File D1, Senior Accountable Official, USAspending.gov

plain_summary: A formal sign-off that an agency's data is complete and accurate. For FPDS, each agency certifies its prior fiscal year's contract data to GSA within 120 days of year end. For the DATA Act, the SAO gives a quarterly assurance.
why_it_matters_here: A certification says the agency checked its data. It does not prove any single row in our files is right.
official_definition: an annual certification of whether, and to what degree, agency CAR data for the preceding fiscal year is complete and accurate.
related_terms: verification and validation, Senior Accountable Official, contract action report, FPDS, GSA

plain_summary: The file that records each team decision about a flag, column or value, with its status, rationale, who decided and when. The dashboard's Decision log page is the only thing that writes it.
why_it_matters_here: Stage 3 may change or leave out a row only by a rule in this log.
related_terms: Stage 3, exclusions ledger, flag

plain_summary: In FPDS terms, any reported contract that is not an IDV. It is award type D in our data.
why_it_matters_here: Definitive contracts and purchase orders stand alone, so they should have no parent IDV (flag G02).
official_definition: any contract that must be reported to FPDS other than an indefinite delivery vehicle
related_terms: IDV, purchase order, award type

plain_summary: An order for goods placed under an existing contract. FPDS uses award type C for both delivery orders and task orders under an IDV.
why_it_matters_here: Delivery orders rose from 1.23 million in FY2014 to 2.87 million in FY2015, the core of the FY2015 row-count jump.
official_definition: Delivery order means an order for supplies placed against an established contract or with Government sources.
related_terms: task order, IDIQ, IDV, award type, row-count jump

plain_summary: An Award Data Archive file that holds only the rows added, changed or deleted since the previous month's files. A column marks each row as changed (C), deleted (D) or added (blank).
why_it_matters_here: We do not use Delta files, so nothing in our data is patched on top of a Full file.
official_definition: only new, modified, and deleted data since the date the last month's files were generated.
pinpoint: Award Data Archive page, archive file types
related_terms: Full file, Award Data Archive, release date

plain_summary: Money taken back from an award, recorded as a negative amount. Early terminations, unused funds and corrections all show up this way.
why_it_matters_here: Deobligations larger than an award's obligations that year sit in 99.0% of negative vendor-cells (582,703 of 588,645), so they are the main source of negative vendor totals.
official_definition: An agency’s cancellation or downward adjustment of previously incurred obligations.
related_terms: obligation, negative vendor total, vendor-cell, reversal pair

plain_summary: The Defense Department's own additions to the FAR.
why_it_matters_here: DFARS rules shape how Defense, the largest buyer in our data, reports to FPDS.
official_definition: DoD implementation and supplementation of the FAR is issued in the Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS) under authorization and subject to the authority, direction, and control of the Secretary of Defense.
related_terms: FAR, DoD 90-day delay

plain_summary: A code that tracks spending from disaster or emergency funding laws, such as COVID-19 relief or the infrastructure law.
why_it_matters_here: It flags awards paid partly with emergency money, which can explain a one-year spike in a cell.
official_definition: Disaster Emergency Fund Code (DEFC) is used to track the spending of funding for disasters and emergencies such as COVID-19.
pinpoint: USAspending glossary, term 'Disaster Emergency Fund Code (DEFC)'
related_terms: national interest action code, appropriation, outlay

plain_summary: Contract data for the Department of Defense and the Army Corps of Engineers is published 90 days after the action. Other agencies' data reaches USAspending about two days after it enters FPDS.
why_it_matters_here: Recent months fill in late, so FY2026 stays incomplete until about January. That is one reason FY2026 is out of scope.
official_definition: Procurement data (such as for contracts and indefinite delivery vehicles (IDV)) for the Department of Defense (DOD) and U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) are published on a 90-day delay
pinpoint: USAspending About the Data, 'Delay in DOD Procurement Data'
related_terms: late-reported row, FPDS, File D1

plain_summary: A database program that runs inside Python and reads Parquet files directly, using SQL, the standard language for database queries.
why_it_matters_here: It runs the Parquet side of the Stage 1 proof and all Stage 2 checks.
official_definition: DuckDB is a relational (table-oriented) DBMS that supports the Structured Query Language (SQL)
related_terms: Parquet, Stage 1, Stage 2

also_called: DUNS number, Data Universal Numbering System, recipient_duns
plain_summary: The 9-digit company ID from Dun & Bradstreet that the government used for vendors until April 2022.
why_it_matters_here: recipient_duns is 21% blank in FY2020, 82% in FY2022 and 100% in FY2023 to FY2025, so we group vendors by UEI.
official_definition: It is a unique 9-digit identification number assigned to a company or organization by Dun & Bradstreet, Inc.
related_terms: UEI, parent DUNS, SAM.gov

plain_summary: The online copy of all federal regulations, including the FAR, updated daily. Legal research should be checked against the official edition.
why_it_matters_here: It is the quickest way to read the FAR as of a past date when checking a threshold.
official_definition: The Electronic Code of Federal Regulations (eCFR) is a web version of the Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) that we update daily to better reflect its current status.
pinpoint: eCFR Reader Aids, What is the eCFR
related_terms: Federal Register, FAR

plain_summary: The number of equal-sized firms that would give the same HHI. With shares as fractions it is 1 divided by HHI, or 10,000 divided by HHI on the 0 to 10,000 scale. An HHI of 2,000 means about 5 equal firms.
why_it_matters_here: It turns HHI into a count that is easier to explain for each cell.
pinpoint: Merger Guidelines (2023), Guideline 1, footnote 13 (five equal firms give an HHI of 2,000)
related_terms: HHI, top-4 share

plain_summary: The one reversal pair that crosses fiscal years. Army contract W912QR08C0053 records +$13.92 billion on 2008-09-29 and -$13.90 billion on 2009-01-07.
why_it_matters_here: It makes Emerson hold most of a 1,039-vendor FY2008 cell (HHI 4,281.8 against 167.2 without it) and drives the FY2009 cell negative.
related_terms: reversal pair, total dollars obligated, negative vendor total, cell

plain_summary: The planned record of every row left out of the working set, each with a reason code. Working set plus ledger must equal Stage 1, in rows and dollars, for every fiscal year.
why_it_matters_here: Nothing can quietly drop out of the concentration measure.
related_terms: Stage 3, decision log, reversal pair

plain_summary: A code for how much competition an award had. A is full and open, B not available for competition, C not competed, D full and open after exclusion of sources, E follow-on to a competed action, F competed under simplified acquisition, G not competed under simplified acquisition.
why_it_matters_here: It is the proposed main competition measure. It is 16.7% blank in FY2008 and under 2% blank from FY2011.
official_definition: A code that represents the competitive nature of the contract.
pinpoint: USAspending glossary, term 'Extent Competed', official text
related_terms: full and open competition, full and open after exclusion of sources, not competed, number of offers received, simplified acquisition threshold

plain_summary: The rule that each holder of a multiple-award contract gets a fair chance at each order above the micro-purchase threshold, unless a legal exception applies.
why_it_matters_here: fair_opportunity_limited_sources_code records which exception, if any, was used on an order.
official_definition: The contracting officer must provide each awardee a fair opportunity to be considered for each order exceeding the micro-purchase threshold issued under multiple delivery-order contracts or multiple task-order contracts
related_terms: multiple award, extent competed, micro-purchase threshold, contracting officer

plain_summary: The main rulebook for how federal agencies buy goods and services. Agencies add their own supplements, such as the DFARS for Defense.
why_it_matters_here: FAR rules set what must be reported to FPDS and the dollar thresholds behind our row-count steps.
official_definition: The Federal Acquisition Regulations System consists of the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR), which is the primary document, and agency acquisition regulations that implement or supplement the FAR.
related_terms: DFARS, FAR subpart 4.6, Federal Acquisition Circular, eCFR

plain_summary: The FAR rules on what agencies must, may and must not report to FPDS, and how fast. Section 4.606 lists what is left out, such as classified actions and most purchases at or below the micro-purchase threshold.
why_it_matters_here: It defines which federal buying can never appear in our data.
official_definition: This subpart prescribes uniform reporting requirements for the Federal Procurement Data System (FPDS).
related_terms: FPDS, FAR, contract action, micro-purchase threshold, government purchase card

plain_summary: A group of Treasury accounts that share an agency code and an account number. USAspending uses it to group related accounts.
why_it_matters_here: federal_accounts_funding_this_award lists the federal accounts that paid for an award. We do not use it in the measure.
official_definition: On this website we group them by their agency identifier (3-digit code) and Main Account code (4-digit code).
related_terms: Treasury Account Symbol, CGAC

plain_summary: A numbered release of FAR changes, such as FAC 2020-07, which raised the micro-purchase threshold to $10,000.
why_it_matters_here: Our micro-purchase threshold dates cite FACs, such as FAC 2005-83 for the $3,500 threshold.
official_definition: Federal Acquisition Circular (FAC) 2005-62, which amends the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR).
related_terms: FAR, Federal Register, micro-purchase threshold

plain_summary: The dollar amount on one transaction row. It is positive for new money and negative for money taken back.
why_it_matters_here: It is the only amount we sum. All 88.7 million rows net to $10.51 trillion.
official_definition: Amount of Federal Government’s obligation, de-obligation, or liability, in dollars, for an award transaction.
pinpoint: USAspending glossary, term 'Federal Action Obligation', official text
related_terms: obligation, deobligation, net dollars, gross dollars

plain_summary: The government's daily publication of new rules, proposed rules and notices. FAR changes are published there and cited by volume and page, such as 80 FR 38293.
why_it_matters_here: Our threshold dates come from Federal Register notices.
official_definition: The Federal Register (the daily journal of the Federal government) is published every business day by the National Archives and Records Administration (NARA)'s Office of the Federal Register (OFR).
related_terms: eCFR, Federal Acquisition Circular, FAR

plain_summary: The 4-digit product classes, such as 1510 for fixed-wing aircraft, kept by the Defense Logistics Agency. Product PSCs are these classes, and the first two digits give the product group.
why_it_matters_here: Cutting the PSC to 2 characters groups products by these groups. That cuts negative vendor-cells from 588,645 to 449,217.
pinpoint: PSC Manual, revision chart (product codes follow the DLA class list) and Section D, Product Codes
related_terms: PSC, market definition

also_called: FSS, Multiple Award Schedule, MAS, GSA Schedule
plain_summary: GSA's program of long-term contracts with set prices that any agency can order from.
why_it_matters_here: Orders under schedules appear as delivery orders or BPA calls whose parent IDV has type C.
official_definition: The Federal Supply Schedule program is also known as the GSA Schedules Program or the Multiple Award Schedule Program.
related_terms: IDV, GSA, BPA, multiple award

also_called: Federal Funding Accountability and Transparency Act of 2006, Pub. L. 109-282
plain_summary: A 2006 law that created USAspending.gov and requires agencies to publish data on federal awards. The DATA Act later expanded it.
why_it_matters_here: It is the legal basis for the public contract data we download.
official_definition: Establishes USAspending.gov and requires agencies to publish data on federal awards equal to or greater than $25,000.
pinpoint: Table 1, Laws and Regulations with Relevant USAspending.gov Reporting Requirements (PDF p. 2, no printed page number)
related_terms: DATA Act, USAspending.gov, File F

plain_summary: The agency file of account balances for the fiscal year to date, by Treasury account. It comes from the agency's accounting system.
why_it_matters_here: Our contract rows come from File D1, so File A is context only.
official_definition: File A contains the FY cumulative appropriations account summary data.
pinpoint: Results in Brief, p. i (PDF p. 3)
related_terms: File B, File C, GTAS, Treasury Account Symbol, appropriation

also_called: Object Class and Program Activity file
plain_summary: The agency file that splits File A's account balances by object class and program activity.
why_it_matters_here: Our contract rows come from File D1, so File B is context only.
official_definition: File B contains the appropriation account data listed in File A but is further defined by object class code and program activity name.
pinpoint: Results in Brief, p. i (PDF p. 3)
related_terms: File A, File C, object class, program activity

also_called: Award Financial file, Account Breakdown by Award
plain_summary: The agency file that lists award-level spending from the agency's accounting system. It is the link between accounts and awards.
why_it_matters_here: The account columns in our files, such as treasury_accounts_funding_this_award, depend on this link. Awards with no link have those columns blank.
official_definition: File C contains transaction-level financial data for all procurements and grants processed during the quarter.
pinpoint: Results in Brief, p. i (PDF p. 3)
related_terms: File A, File B, File D1, unlinked award, Treasury Account Symbol

also_called: Procurement file, Award and Awardee Attributes (Procurement)
plain_summary: The DATA Act file of contract award data that the Broker builds from FPDS. It holds the transaction amount, dates, agency, vendor, PSC, NAICS and similar fields.
why_it_matters_here: Our contract files are built from File D1 data, so its coverage limits are our coverage limits.
official_definition: File D1 contains procurement award and awardee data extracted from the Federal Procurement Data System-Next Generation.
pinpoint: Results in Brief, p. ii (PDF p. 4)
related_terms: FPDS, File C, File D2, DATA Act Broker, DoD 90-day delay

plain_summary: The DATA Act file of grants, loans and other financial assistance. It is the assistance counterpart of File D1.
why_it_matters_here: Out of scope. We use contracts only.
official_definition: File D2 contains grant award and awardee data extracted from the Financial Assistance Broker Submission system on grant and other financial assistance awards.
pinpoint: Results in Brief, p. ii (PDF p. 4)
related_terms: File D1, DATA Act Broker

also_called: Additional Awardee Data file, executive compensation file
plain_summary: The DATA Act file of extra recipient data taken from SAM.gov, such as the pay of a recipient's top five executives.
why_it_matters_here: Our files carry these executive pay columns, but we do not use them.
official_definition: File E includes information extracted from System for Award Management on the award recipients.
pinpoint: Results in Brief, p. ii (PDF p. 4)
related_terms: SAM.gov, File F, DATA Act Broker

plain_summary: The DATA Act file of subawards, the contracts or grants that a main award holder passes on to other firms. The main award holders report them.
why_it_matters_here: Out of scope. Our measure counts prime contract dollars only, so money passed to subcontractors stays with the prime vendor.
official_definition: File F contains information extracted from the FFATA Sub-award Reporting System on awards made to sub-recipients under a prime contract or grant award.
pinpoint: Results in Brief, p. ii (PDF p. 4)
related_terms: File E, FFATA, DATA Act Broker

plain_summary: The federal budget year. It runs from October 1 to September 30 and is named for the year it ends, so FY2025 began on 2024-10-01.
why_it_matters_here: Every cell is one fiscal year, assigned from action_date.
where_it_shows_up: action_date_fiscal_year, file names FY2008 to FY2025
official_definition: For the federal government, it runs from October 1 to September 30.
related_terms: action date, cell

plain_summary: A fact recorded about a row, year or code, such as a PSC that is not 4 characters. Each flag has a fixed rule and a severity of serious, review or info.
why_it_matters_here: Flags mark rows for team decisions without changing them.
related_terms: flag catalog, Stage 2, decision log

plain_summary: The list of every integrity rule with its threshold and severity. It holds 62 flags, 61 committed before the first run plus F10, which was added later and disclosed.
why_it_matters_here: Fixing the rules before seeing the data keeps the checks from being tuned to the results.
related_terms: flag, Stage 2, decision log

also_called: FPDS-NG, Federal Procurement Data System, Federal Procurement Data System-Next Generation
plain_summary: The government-wide database where contracting officers report each contract action. GSA manages it. USAspending copies its contract data from FPDS.
why_it_matters_here: Every row in our data began as an FPDS record, so any gap or error in FPDS is also in our data.
official_definition: The FPDS provides a comprehensive web-based tool for agencies to report contract actions
related_terms: File D1, contract action, contract action report, FAR subpart 4.6, USAspending.gov, GSA, contracting officer

plain_summary: A 4-character agency code that USAspending uses for some agencies in place of a 3-character CGAC code. Eleven agencies in our data use one, such as 1601 for Labor and 3300 for the Smithsonian.
why_it_matters_here: No agency appears under both a 3- and a 4-character code (flag F10), so no market is split in two.
official_definition: The toptier code of an agency (could be a CGAC or FREC) so only numeric character strings of length 3-4 are accepted.
related_terms: CGAC, awarding agency

term: full and open after exclusion of sources
also_called: extent_competed_code D, full and open competition after exclusion of sources
plain_summary: Competition open to everyone in a defined group, with other sources left out on purpose. Small business set-asides are the usual case.
why_it_matters_here: Code D actions are competed, but only among a subset of firms, which caps how many vendors a cell can have.
official_definition: This subpart prescribes policies and procedures for providing for full and open competition after excluding one or more sources.
related_terms: set-aside, extent competed, full and open competition

plain_summary: Competition in which every capable, eligible firm may bid.
why_it_matters_here: Code A is the baseline for competitive markets in our data.
official_definition: when used with respect to a contract action, means that all responsible sources are permitted to compete.
pinpoint: FAR 2.101(b), definition of full and open competition
related_terms: extent competed, full and open after exclusion of sources, other than full and open competition

plain_summary: An Award Data Archive file that holds every transaction for one fiscal year as of the day the file was built.
why_it_matters_here: We load Full files only, so each fiscal year in our data is one complete snapshot.
official_definition: data for the fiscal year up until the date the file was prepared
pinpoint: Award Data Archive page, archive file types
related_terms: Delta file, Award Data Archive, release date

plain_summary: The agency that paid most of the money for an award. It is often the same as the awarding agency.
why_it_matters_here: Funding agency code 999 covers 46.86% of FY2008 rows, so funding-agency analysis is reliable only from FY2011.
official_definition: Name and 3-digit CGAC agency code of the department or establishment of the Government that provided the preponderance of the funds for an award and/or individual transactions related to an award.
pinpoint: USAspending glossary, term 'Funding Agency', official text
related_terms: awarding agency, funding agency 999, CGAC

plain_summary: A placeholder funding agency code with a blank name. It covers 46.86% of FY2008 rows, 32.26% in FY2009, 11.14% in FY2010 and fewer than 200 rows a year from FY2012.
why_it_matters_here: It makes funding-agency analysis unreliable before FY2011, so the main measure uses the awarding agency.
related_terms: funding agency, awarding agency

plain_summary: The independent, nonpartisan audit agency that works for Congress.
why_it_matters_here: GAO's yearly contract totals are our primary benchmark for FY2018 to FY2025, and its audits are the main record of known data problems.
official_definition: GAO, often called the "congressional watchdog,” is an independent, non-partisan agency that works for Congress.
related_terms: benchmark, inspector general, CIGIE

plain_summary: One ID that stands for a whole category of vendors instead of one firm. The FAR allows it for some small awards and for some vendors outside the United States.
why_it_matters_here: Placeholder vendors such as MISCELLANEOUS FOREIGN AWARDEES work like this, so one vendor ID can cover many firms.
official_definition: Generic entity identifier means a number or other identifier assigned to a category of vendors and not specific to any individual or entity.
pinpoint: FAR 4.601, definition, uses listed in FAR 4.605(c)(2)
related_terms: MISCELLANEOUS FOREIGN AWARDEES, placeholder vendor, UEI

also_called: purchase card, Governmentwide commercial purchase card, GPC
plain_summary: A government credit card that staff use to buy and pay for small purchases.
why_it_matters_here: Card buys below the micro-purchase threshold are generally not reported to FPDS (FAR 4.606(c)(1)), so most card spending is outside our data.
official_definition: Governmentwide commercial purchase card means a purchase card, similar in nature to a commercial credit card, issued to authorized agency personnel to use to acquire and to pay for supplies and services.
related_terms: micro-purchase, micro-purchase threshold, FAR subpart 4.6

plain_summary: The sum of the absolute values of the amounts, so a +$5 entry and a -$5 reversal count as $10.
why_it_matters_here: Reversal pairs distort gross totals badly. The FY2013 pair alone is 5.4% of the $12.82 trillion gross over 18 years.
related_terms: net dollars, reversal pair

plain_summary: The agency that runs government-wide buying programs such as the Federal Supply Schedules. Its Integrated Award Environment office manages FPDS.
why_it_matters_here: GSA runs the system our data comes from, and its yearly FPDS totals are our context benchmark.
pinpoint: GAO-25-107469, p. 26 (PDF p. 31), on GSA's Integrated Award Environment program office managing FPDS
related_terms: FPDS, SAM.gov, Federal Supply Schedule, benchmark

also_called: Governmentwide Treasury Account Symbol Adjusted Trial Balance System
plain_summary: Treasury's system where agencies report their account balances and their spending against their budgets. Agency File A is checked against it.
why_it_matters_here: It ties agency books to spending reports. It does not hold our contract rows.
official_definition: Entities, including agencies, use GTAS to provide proprietary financial reporting information and information about budget execution to the Department of the Treasury.
related_terms: File A, Treasury Account Symbol, DATA Act

also_called: governmentwide acquisition contract, government-wide acquisition contract
plain_summary: An IDV for information technology that one agency sets up for every agency to use.
why_it_matters_here: Each order under a GWAC carries its own awarding agency, so GWAC spending spreads across many agencies' cells.
official_definition: a task-order or delivery-order contract for information technology established by one agency for Governmentwide use
pinpoint: FAR 2.101(b), definition of Governmentwide acquisition contract
related_terms: IDV, multi-agency contract, task order, delivery order

plain_summary: A score from near 0 to 10,000 for how concentrated a market is. Square each firm's percentage share and add the squares. One firm with everything scores 10,000.
why_it_matters_here: It is the project's main measure, computed per cell from vendors' net dollars.
official_definition: The HHI is calculated by squaring the market share of each firm competing in the market and then summing the resulting numbers.
pinpoint: DOJ Antitrust Division, Herfindahl-Hirschman Index page
related_terms: top-4 share, effective number of firms, HHI thresholds (2023 guidelines), HHI thresholds (2010 guidelines), market definition, vendor-cell

plain_summary: Under the 2010 guidelines, HHI below 1,500 was unconcentrated, 1,500 to 2,500 moderately concentrated and above 2,500 highly concentrated. A rise of more than 200 points in a highly concentrated market was presumed harmful.
why_it_matters_here: Results for FY2008 to FY2023 may be read against these older bands, which are looser than the 2023 ones.
official_definition: Mergers resulting in highly concentrated markets that involve an increase in the HHI of more than 200 points will be presumed to be likely to enhance market power.
pinpoint: Horizontal Merger Guidelines (2010), Section 5.3, p. 19 (PDF p. 22)
related_terms: HHI, HHI thresholds (2023 guidelines)

plain_summary: Under the 2023 Merger Guidelines of the Department of Justice and the Federal Trade Commission, a market with HHI above 1,800 is highly concentrated, and a rise of more than 100 points is significant.
why_it_matters_here: Comparing cell HHIs with 1,800 gives a familiar yardstick, though the guidelines were written for mergers.
official_definition: Markets with an HHI greater than 1,800 are highly concentrated, and a change of more than 100 points is a significant increase.
related_terms: HHI, HHI thresholds (2010 guidelines)

plain_summary: An SBA program for small firms based in economically distressed areas, called HUBZones. SBA certifies these firms.
why_it_matters_here: HUBZone set-asides limit who can bid, which can shape concentration in a cell.
official_definition: HUBZone means a historically underutilized business zone that is an area located within one or more qualified census tracts, qualified nonmetropolitan counties, lands within the external boundaries of an Indian reservation, qualified base closure areas, redesignated areas, governor-designated covered areas, or qualified disaster areas
related_terms: set-aside, SBA, small business concern

also_called: indefinite-delivery, indefinite-quantity contract, indefinite-quantity contract, IDC
plain_summary: A contract that sets a minimum and maximum amount over a period. The agency buys the actual work through orders.
why_it_matters_here: Order rows in our data link to their IDIQ contract or other IDV through parent_award_id_piid.
official_definition: An indefinite-quantity contract provides for an indefinite quantity, within stated limits, of supplies or services during a fixed period. The Government places orders for individual requirements.
related_terms: IDV, delivery order, task order, multiple award

also_called: indefinite delivery vehicle, contract vehicle, umbrella agreement
plain_summary: An umbrella contract or agreement under which agencies later place orders. Types include GWACs, IDIQ contracts, Federal Supply Schedules, BOAs and BPAs. IDV rows usually carry no dollars, and the orders under them do.
why_it_matters_here: IDV rows that carry dollars (flag D04) number 183,497 with $197.7 billion net. We keep them in totals because the GAO match includes them.
official_definition: Indefinite Delivery Vehicles (IDVs) are vehicles that facilitate the delivery of supply and service orders.
related_terms: IDIQ, GWAC, Federal Supply Schedule, BPA, BOA, referenced IDV, US Mint rows

also_called: IG, OIG, Office of Inspector General
plain_summary: An independent office inside an agency that audits and investigates that agency. IGs have audited their agencies' DATA Act data.
why_it_matters_here: IG audits give error rates for agency contract data, the closest thing to a field-by-field accuracy check.
official_definition: established agency inspectors general to provide policy direction for and to conduct, supervise, and coordinate audits and investigations relating to agency programs and operations.
pinpoint: Budget Glossary, Appendix I, p. 113 (PDF p. 117)
related_terms: CIGIE, GAO, DATA Act

also_called: code and label drift, flags F07 and F08
plain_summary: A code whose text label changes within a year or across years, such as an agency renamed.
why_it_matters_here: Grouping by codes avoids splitting one agency or PSC into several groups.
related_terms: awarding agency, PSC, cell

plain_summary: A period when Congress has not passed funding for an agency, often called a shutdown. Agencies can then make only the obligations the law still allows.
why_it_matters_here: The fall 2025 lapse began in FY2026, after our years end. A 2019 lapse pushed back a DATA Act deadline (GAO-20-540), so lapses can slow data updates.
official_definition: under a lapse in appropriations, agencies could not incur any obligation that was not legally funded from prior appropriations or otherwise authorized by law.
pinpoint: GSA Order ADM 4220.1S, Operations in the absence of appropriations, p. 6 (PDF p. 6)
related_terms: appropriation, obligation, fiscal year

also_called: flag C07, reported more than 90 days after the action
plain_summary: A row first reported more than 90 days after its action date.
why_it_matters_here: Late rows cluster by agency and year, such as 884,941 GSA Federal Acquisition Service rows in FY2019, so recent months can still be filling in.
related_terms: DoD 90-day delay, action date, release date

plain_summary: The Parquet files that make up Stage 1, one per comma-separated data file inside each zip. Every column is text, and three extra columns record each row's exact place in the zip.
why_it_matters_here: Reading Layer A gives the published values with nothing changed. Read it through _files.json, never with a wildcard, to avoid double counting.
related_terms: Stage 1, Layer B, lineage columns, Parquet

plain_summary: The FY2025 pilot's typed table of 32 chosen columns, with money as exact decimals and dates as dates. It is not rebuilt in the all-years work.
why_it_matters_here: It shows how the later working set will type columns. Codes stay text so leading zeros survive.
related_terms: Layer A, Stage 3

plain_summary: Three columns added to each Layer A row that record which file inside the zip it came from and its row number there.
why_it_matters_here: Any row can be traced back to its exact place in the published zip.
related_terms: Layer A, Stage 1, Stage 0

plain_summary: The file with one row per source zip, holding its SHA-256, path, web address, row count and dollar total.
why_it_matters_here: It proves which exact files every number came from.
related_terms: SHA-256, Stage 0, release date

plain_summary: Deciding which sellers and products count as one market before measuring shares. Our market is one cell, meaning one awarding agency, one PSC and one fiscal year.
why_it_matters_here: Concentration scores change with the market definition. Cutting PSC to 2 characters or using NAICS gives different answers.
official_definition: First, market definition helps specify the line of commerce and section of the country in which the competitive concern arises.
pinpoint: Horizontal Merger Guidelines (2010), Section 4, p. 7 (PDF p. 10)
related_terms: cell, PSC, NAICS, HHI

plain_summary: An older fingerprint method that turns any input into a 128-bit code.
why_it_matters_here: The row fingerprint uses MD5 to compare all 297 fields of every row.
official_definition: algorithm takes as input a message of arbitrary length and produces as output a 128-bit "fingerprint" or "message digest" of the input.
related_terms: row fingerprint, SHA-256

plain_summary: A small purchase at or below the micro-purchase threshold, often paid with a government purchase card. Agencies need not report most of them to FPDS.
why_it_matters_here: Reporting below the threshold is optional, so changes in what agencies report can create row-count steps with almost no dollars behind them.
official_definition: an acquisition of supplies or services using simplified acquisition procedures
related_terms: micro-purchase threshold, government purchase card, FAR subpart 4.6, row-count jump

plain_summary: The dollar limit for a micro-purchase. It was $3,000 for FY2008 to FY2015 and $3,500 from FY2016. It rose to $10,000 in the FAR on 2020-08-31 and to $15,000 on 2025-10-01.
why_it_matters_here: FPDS must hold actions above the threshold, so each change can shift how many small rows appear.
official_definition: Micro-purchase threshold means $15,000
pinpoint: FAR 2.101(b), definition of micro-purchase threshold (text as retrieved 2026-10-06)
related_terms: micro-purchase, simplified acquisition threshold, Federal Acquisition Circular, row-count jump

plain_summary: A placeholder vendor name that stands for many foreign companies, almost all on Defense contracts. One vendor ID carries 974,811 of its 974,817 rows and $41.21 billion.
why_it_matters_here: Scored as one company it would hold more than 10% of net dollars in 18,995 cells. The proposal is to report it separately and leave it out of HHI.
related_terms: placeholder vendor, generic entity identifier, vendor

plain_summary: A change to an existing contract, such as adding money, exercising an option or ending the contract early. Each modification is its own row with its own amount, which can be negative.
why_it_matters_here: Modifications carry deobligations and reversal pairs. In FY2025, modification 0 is 80.8% of rows but only 41.3% of dollars.
official_definition: The identifier of an action being reported that indicates the specific subsequent change to the initial award.
related_terms: transaction, deobligation, option, reversal pair

plain_summary: An order contract that one agency sets up for other agencies to use.
why_it_matters_here: Each order under a MAC carries its own awarding agency, so MAC spending spreads across many agencies' cells.
official_definition: A Multi-Agency Contract (MAC) is a task-order or delivery-order contract established by one agency for use by government agencies to obtain supplies and services.
related_terms: GWAC, IDV, awarding agency

plain_summary: An IDV awarded to several vendors from one competition. The vendors then compete for each order.
why_it_matters_here: Orders under multiple-award IDVs are competed through fair opportunity, so their competition codes differ from those of standalone contracts.
official_definition: Indicates whether the contract is one of many that resulted from a single solicitation, all of the contracts are for the same or similar items, and contracting officers are required to compare their requirements with the offerings under more than one contract or are required to acquire the requirement competitively among the awardees.
related_terms: fair opportunity, IDIQ, IDV, extent competed

also_called: North American Industry Classification System, naics_code
plain_summary: A 6-digit industry code. The contracting officer picks one for each contract, and it sets which small business size standard applies.
why_it_matters_here: NAICS is an alternative market definition. It is 19.7% blank in FY2008 and under 2% blank from FY2011, and its codes are revised every 5 years.
official_definition: The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) is the standard used by Federal statistical agencies in classifying business establishments for the purpose of collecting, analyzing, and publishing statistical data related to the U.S. business economy.
pinpoint: Census NAICS page, Introduction to NAICS
related_terms: PSC, small business size standard, market definition, contracting officer

plain_summary: A code that tags contracts tied to a declared emergency or national event, such as a named hurricane or COVID-19.
why_it_matters_here: It can explain a one-year spike in a cell, such as COVID-19 buying in FY2020. FPDS end-dated the field as of 2024-01-27.
official_definition: The National Interest Action values are used to categorize procurement actions related to emergency contingency responses or other nationally significant events.
pinpoint: USAspending glossary, term 'National Interest Action (NIA)', official text
related_terms: Disaster Emergency Fund Code

plain_summary: A vendor-cell whose net is below zero, usually because money obligated in an earlier year was taken back.
why_it_matters_here: A negative total has no meaningful share. 588,645 vendor-cells (7.5%) are negative, in 35.0% of cells, netting to -$124.05 billion.
related_terms: vendor-cell, deobligation, cell, HHI

plain_summary: The sum of all amounts with their signs, so a +$5 entry and a -$5 reversal net to $0.
why_it_matters_here: Vendor shares, HHI and CR4 use net dollars per vendor-cell. All years net to $10.51 trillion.
related_terms: gross dollars, federal action obligation, vendor-cell, HHI

plain_summary: Dollar amounts as recorded at the time, with no adjustment for inflation.
why_it_matters_here: All our totals are nominal. GAO's charts state constant-dollar figures, which equal nominal only in the chart's base year.
official_definition: The current dollar value of a good or service is its value in terms of prices current at the time the good or service is acquired or sold.
related_terms: constant dollars, benchmark

also_called: extent_competed_code B, C and G, sole source
plain_summary: An award made without competition. Codes B (not available for competition), C (not competed) and G (not competed under simplified acquisition) mark it.
why_it_matters_here: Cells with many uncompeted awards can show high concentration for legal reasons, such as only one capable source.
pinpoint: USAspending glossary, term 'Extent Competed', plain text (code list)
related_terms: extent competed, other than full and open competition

plain_summary: How many bids or proposals came in for the award.
why_it_matters_here: It is 5% blank or less through FY2017 and 63% to 70% blank from FY2018. Zero offers on a competed action (flag X02) seems to mean not reported in FY2008 to FY2011.
official_definition: The number of actual offers/bids received in response to the solicitation.
related_terms: extent competed, full and open competition

plain_summary: A budget category for what money was spent on, such as personnel pay or equipment, whatever the agency or program.
why_it_matters_here: object_classes_funding_this_award shows the budget categories behind an award. We do not use it in the measure.
official_definition: Categories in a classification system that presents obligations by the items or services purchased by the Federal Government.
pinpoint: USAspending glossary, term 'Object Class', official text
related_terms: program activity, File B, obligation

plain_summary: A binding promise to pay, made when an agency signs a contract or places an order. Payment can come right away or years later.
why_it_matters_here: Our measure counts obligations. Payments made later are outlays, a separate figure.
official_definition: Obligation means a legally binding agreement that will result in outlays, immediately or in the future.
related_terms: federal action obligation, deobligation, outlay, appropriation

plain_summary: The White House office that prepares the budget and oversees how agencies are managed. It sets rules for procurement data quality and DATA Act reporting.
why_it_matters_here: OMB guidance set the verification and validation and SAO rules behind the data we use.
official_definition: Specifically, OMB’s mission is to assist the President in meeting his policy, budget, management and regulatory objectives and to fulfill the agency’s statutory responsibilities.
related_terms: verification and validation, Senior Accountable Official, DATA Act

plain_summary: A right written into a contract that lets the government buy more or extend the contract later.
why_it_matters_here: Exercising an option is a modification that can add an obligation row.
official_definition: Option means a unilateral right in a contract by which, for a specified time, the Government may elect to purchase additional supplies or services called for by the contract, or may elect to extend the term of the contract.
related_terms: modification, base and exercised options value, base and all options value

term: other than full and open competition
plain_summary: The legal exceptions that let an agency skip full and open competition, such as only one responsible source or unusual urgency.
why_it_matters_here: other_than_full_and_open_competition_code gives the reason for an uncompeted award.
official_definition: The designator for solicitation procedures other than full and open competition pursuant to FAR 6.3.
related_terms: not competed, full and open competition, extent competed

plain_summary: A legally binding agreement that is neither a standard contract nor a grant. Agencies use OTAs for flexible deals such as research and prototypes.
why_it_matters_here: FAR 4.601 leaves other transactions out of contract actions, so OTA dollars may be missing from our cells. GAO found agencies reported OTA spending inconsistently.
official_definition: other transaction agreements (OTA)—legally binding agreements other than standard federal contracts and grants, allowing for more flexible arrangements.
related_terms: contract action, FPDS, GAO

plain_summary: Money actually paid out to settle an obligation. It can come years after the obligation.
why_it_matters_here: Our files carry an award-level outlay column, but outlays were required only from FY2022 except for COVID-19 awards, so we do not use it.
official_definition: The issuance of checks, disbursement of cash, or electronic transfer of funds made to liquidate a federal obligation.
related_terms: obligation, Disaster Emergency Fund Code

plain_summary: The DUNS number of a vendor's ultimate parent, used before April 2022.
why_it_matters_here: It is empty in recent years, so the parent UEI is the only parent ID that spans FY2008 to FY2025.
official_definition: The unique identification number for the ultimate parent of an awardee or recipient.
related_terms: DUNS, parent UEI, ultimate parent

plain_summary: Our check of whether the parent ID on a row changes when a deal closes or carries today's parent back in time. Four deals from 2013 to 2020 were tested against closing dates in company filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission.
why_it_matters_here: In all four the parent ID switched 2 to 6 months after closing, which supports using the parent recorded at the time of each action.
related_terms: parent UEI, ultimate parent, vendor

plain_summary: The UEI of a vendor's ultimate parent company.
why_it_matters_here: Our vendor is the parent UEI, or the recipient UEI where the parent is blank. The parent test found the parent ID switches 2 to 6 months after a deal closes.
official_definition: The Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) for the ultimate parent of an awardee or recipient.
related_terms: UEI, ultimate parent, vendor, parent test

plain_summary: An open file format that stores data by column, which makes large tables fast to read.
why_it_matters_here: Stage 1 holds all 18 years as 97 Parquet files, 19.84 GB in total.
official_definition: Apache Parquet is an open source, column-oriented data file format designed for efficient data storage and retrieval.
related_terms: Layer A, DuckDB, Stage 1

plain_summary: The status of a benchmark check. PASS means within 2% of the published total, WARN within 10% and FAIL beyond 10%. The bands were fixed before any comparison.
why_it_matters_here: All 8 benchmarked years PASS under the version 2 rule.
related_terms: benchmark, benchmark figure, benchmark bound

plain_summary: The dates the contract work runs, from the start date to the current end date. The end date counts exercised options only.
why_it_matters_here: 2,229,493 rows show a start date after the end date (flag C06). Most are modifications before FY2020 that carry their own date as the start.
official_definition: The date that the award begins, as agreed upon by the parties involved.
pinpoint: USAspending glossary, term 'Period of Performance Start Date'
related_terms: modification, option, action date

also_called: Procurement Instrument Identifier, award ID, contract number
plain_summary: The contract or order number the agency assigns. Agencies must keep each PIID unique government-wide.
why_it_matters_here: award_id_piid is easy to read but is not unique across agencies by itself, so we key awards on contract_award_unique_key.
official_definition: A unique identifier assigned to a federal contract, purchase order, basic ordering agreement, basic agreement, and blanket purchase agreement.
related_terms: unique award key, referenced IDV, award

plain_summary: A vendor name that is a placeholder, such as MULTIPLE RECIPIENTS, UNKNOWN or MISCELLANEOUS FOREIGN AWARDEES, instead of a real firm.
why_it_matters_here: A concentration measure must not treat a placeholder as one company.
related_terms: MISCELLANEOUS FOREIGN AWARDEES, generic entity identifier, vendor

plain_summary: For a contract, the total that could be obligated if the base and all options were used.
why_it_matters_here: It is an award-level ceiling and is never a measure of spending.
official_definition: For procurement, the total amount that could be obligated on a contract, if the base and all options are exercised.
related_terms: base and all options value, option

plain_summary: A specific activity or project inside a budget account, as listed in the President's budget.
why_it_matters_here: program_activities_funding_this_award links an award to the budget programs that paid for it. We do not use it in the measure.
official_definition: A specific activity or project as listed in the program and financing schedules of the annual budget of the United States Government.
pinpoint: USAspending glossary, term 'Program Activity', official text
related_terms: object class, File B, Treasury Account Symbol

plain_summary: A 4-character code for what was bought. Codes that start with a digit are products. Codes that start with a letter are services or research and development.
why_it_matters_here: PSC is the product side of our cell. One revision end-dated 721 research and development codes and added 155, which breaks those series across years.
official_definition: The Product and Service Codes (PSC) Manual provides codes to describe products, services, and research and development (R&D) purchased by the federal government.
related_terms: Federal Supply Class, NAICS, cell, market definition

plain_summary: A simple order to buy goods or services under the simplified acquisition rules. It is award type B in our data.
why_it_matters_here: Purchase orders fell from 1,600,094 in FY2008 to 858,147 in FY2009, part of the FY2008 row-count step.
official_definition: means an offer by the Government to buy supplies or services, including construction and research and development, upon specified terms and conditions, using simplified acquisition procedures
related_terms: simplified acquisition threshold, definitive contract, award type, row-count jump

plain_summary: An internal ID that USAspending gives each recipient profile on its website and its public data service. It ends in -P for a parent, -C for a child company, or -R for neither.
why_it_matters_here: It is not a column in our files. Our vendor grouping uses UEIs.
where_it_shows_up: USAspending recipient profile pages and API (not in our files)
official_definition: A unique identifier for the recipient at a specific level (parent, child, or neither).
related_terms: UEI, parent UEI, ultimate parent

plain_summary: The IDV that an order was placed under. On an order row, parent_award_id_piid holds the IDV's PIID.
why_it_matters_here: Orders link to their IDV through this field. Three orders have no parent and three standalone contracts have one (flags G01 and G02).
official_definition: The identifier of the procurement award under which the specific award is issued, such as a Federal Supply Schedule.
pinpoint: USAspending glossary, term 'Parent Award Identification (ID) Number'
related_terms: IDV, PIID, delivery order, BPA call

plain_summary: The date in an archive zip's name, which marks the snapshot it holds. All our zips come from the 2026-09-06 release.
why_it_matters_here: Every file is a snapshot, and one release for all years avoids small differences nobody could trace (flag A01).
where_it_shows_up: file names *_20260906.zip, data/manifest.csv (data_as_of_date), config/flag_catalog.csv (A01, A02), docs/data_stages.md
related_terms: Full file, Award Data Archive, Stage 0, manifest

also_called: entry and reversal, erroneous entry pair
plain_summary: A very large entry and a matching negative entry on the same contract a few days later, most likely an error and its correction. We found five, from $7.0 billion to $344.7 billion.
why_it_matters_here: Pairs inside one fiscal year cancel in net totals but distort gross totals. The Emerson pair crosses fiscal years and breaks two cells.
related_terms: Emerson pair, gross dollars, net dollars, exclusions ledger, deobligation

plain_summary: One number that sums up every field of every row in a file. Each row's 297 fields are joined and run through MD5, and the first 16 characters of each row's code are added up.
why_it_matters_here: Matching fingerprints on both readers is strong evidence that every field of every row was copied exactly.
related_terms: MD5, Stage 1, Layer A

plain_summary: A sharp change in the number of rows with little change in dollars. Ours occur in FY2008, FY2015 and FY2019, each driven by small orders from one agency.
why_it_matters_here: Counts of actions or vendors step up with no change in spending, so count-based measures need a fixed size cutoff such as $10,000.
related_terms: micro-purchase threshold, delivery order, BPA call, purchase order, subtier agency

plain_summary: The government registry of companies and other entities that want federal awards. Vendors register there to get a UEI. SAM also records each vendor's CAGE code.
why_it_matters_here: The UEI and parent UEI that define our vendors come from SAM registrations.
official_definition: System for Award Management (SAM) which is the primary database for information on entities that do business with the federal government, and in which such entities must register
related_terms: UEI, parent UEI, CAGE code, File E, GSA

plain_summary: The agency that sets small business size standards and runs programs such as 8(a), HUBZone and the women-owned program.
why_it_matters_here: SBA rules decide which vendors count as small, which shapes set-asides in our data.
pinpoint: FAR 19.102(a)(1) (SBA establishes size standards industry by industry)
related_terms: small business size standard, 8(a), HUBZone, WOSB, SDVOSB

plain_summary: A small business at least 51% owned and controlled by veterans with service-connected disabilities.
why_it_matters_here: SDVOSB set-asides limit who can bid, which can shape concentration in a cell.
official_definition: Not less than 51 percent of which is owned and controlled by one or more service-disabled veterans
pinpoint: FAR 2.101(b), definition of SDVOSB concern, paragraph (1)(i)
related_terms: set-aside, small business concern

plain_summary: The official at each agency who signs off on the agency's DATA Act data each quarter.
why_it_matters_here: SAO sign-offs cover File A to File C and the links between files. They do not certify each FPDS row.
official_definition: Each agency’s data must pass a series of validations in the broker and then be certified by the agency’s senior accountable official (SAO) before they are submitted for display on USAspending.gov.
related_terms: DATA Act, data quality certification, DATA Act Broker

plain_summary: An award reserved for a group of firms, usually small businesses or a type of small business such as 8(a) or HUBZone firms.
why_it_matters_here: type_of_set_aside_code is blank on 77% of FY2025 rows, so set-aside analysis needs care.
official_definition: A tool used to award contracts to specific types of businesses. Most set asides reserve contracts for small businesses.
related_terms: small business concern, 8(a), HUBZone, SDVOSB, WOSB, full and open after exclusion of sources

plain_summary: A fingerprint of a file's exact bytes. Changing even one byte gives a different value.
why_it_matters_here: Each zip's SHA-256 in the manifest was checked before and after every move, so Stage 0 is provably unchanged.
official_definition: This Standard specifies secure hash algorithms - SHA-1, SHA-224, SHA-256,
related_terms: MD5, manifest, Stage 0

plain_summary: The dollar limit below which agencies may use simpler, faster buying procedures. It is $350,000 in the current FAR.
why_it_matters_here: Extent competed codes F and G mark actions competed or not competed under these simpler procedures.
official_definition: Simplified acquisition threshold means $350,000
pinpoint: FAR 2.101(b), definition of simplified acquisition threshold (text as retrieved 2026-10-06)
related_terms: micro-purchase threshold, purchase order, extent competed

plain_summary: A firm that is independently owned, does not dominate its field, and is under SBA's size standard for the contract, counting the firms it controls or that control it.
why_it_matters_here: Small business status changes which competition rules apply and is recorded on each row.
official_definition: that is independently owned and operated, not dominant in its field of operation, and qualified as a small business under the criteria and size standards in 13 CFR part 121
pinpoint: FAR 2.101(b), definition of small business concern, paragraph (1)
related_terms: small business size standard, set-aside, SBA

plain_summary: The largest a firm may be, in employees or yearly revenue, and still count as small for a contract. SBA sets one for each NAICS code.
why_it_matters_here: Size is judged per contract, so the same vendor can be small on one row and other than small on another.
official_definition: These size standards define the maximum size that a business — and its affiliates — can be to qualify as a small business for a particular contract.
related_terms: small business concern, NAICS, SBA, set-aside

plain_summary: The zip files exactly as USAspending published them, locked read-only. Everything else is built from them.
why_it_matters_here: It is the fixed starting point that every later number can be traced back to.
related_terms: Stage 1, manifest, SHA-256, release date, Award Data Archive

plain_summary: A lossless copy of every row and all 297 columns in Parquet, with every value kept as text. Two independent readers prove it matches the zips, file by file.
why_it_matters_here: It lets us query 88.7 million rows quickly without trusting a conversion we have not checked.
related_terms: Layer A, Stage 0, Stage 2, row fingerprint, Parquet, DuckDB

plain_summary: Facts about the data kept beside it, such as row flags, per-year profiles and cross-year checks. It changes nothing in Stage 0 or Stage 1 and can be rebuilt at any time.
why_it_matters_here: All integrity findings come from Stage 2.
related_terms: flag, flag catalog, Stage 1, Stage 3

plain_summary: The future typed and cleaned table for analysis. It is not built yet. Rows can be changed or left out only by rules recorded in the decision log.
why_it_matters_here: HHI and CR4 will be computed from Stage 3, and every left-out row will sit in the exclusions ledger.
related_terms: exclusions ledger, decision log, Stage 2

plain_summary: A unit inside an agency, such as the Army or the Defense Logistics Agency inside Defense.
why_it_matters_here: Sub-agencies drive row counts. Defense Logistics Agency rows rose from 600,140 in FY2014 to 2,486,703 in FY2015.
where_it_shows_up: awarding_sub_agency_code, funding_sub_agency_code, config/flag_catalog.csv (F06, H06 to H08), docs/integrity_findings_v3.md
official_definition: Name and identifier of the level 2 organization that awarded, executed or is otherwise responsible for the transaction.
pinpoint: USAspending glossary, term 'Awarding Sub-Agency', official text
related_terms: awarding agency, contracting office, row-count jump

plain_summary: An order for services placed under an existing contract.
why_it_matters_here: FPDS records task orders under an IDV as award type C, the same code as delivery orders, so our data cannot separate them by type.
official_definition: Task order means an order for services placed against an established contract or with Government sources.
related_terms: delivery order, IDIQ, GWAC

plain_summary: A month whose rows or dollars fall below half the median month of its fiscal year.
why_it_matters_here: Only one month in 18 years is thin by dollars, January 2009, and the Emerson reversal alone causes it.
related_terms: Emerson pair, fiscal year

plain_summary: The combined share of the four largest firms in a market, from 0% to 100%.
why_it_matters_here: It is the project's second measure, computed per cell beside HHI.
related_terms: HHI, effective number of firms, cell, vendor

plain_summary: A system total of every row's obligation amount for one contract.
why_it_matters_here: The Emerson award's total, $16,293,527.48, equals the net of all its rows across years, which shows its $13.9 billion entry and reversal cancel out.
related_terms: federal action obligation, Emerson pair, current total value of award

plain_summary: One reported action on an award, either the original award or a later change. Each row in our files is one transaction.
why_it_matters_here: Our 88,753,968 rows are transactions. Counting rows counts actions, which is why small orders can move row counts without moving dollars.
official_definition: A transaction can be the initial contract, grant, loan, or insurance award or any amendment or modification to that award.
related_terms: award, modification, contract action, transaction key

plain_summary: USAspending's ID for one transaction row, built from the agency, PIID, modification number, parent IDV and transaction number.
why_it_matters_here: Flags B01 to B03 test that it is present and unique within and across fiscal years.
official_definition: Derived element and system-generated database key used to uniquely identify each contract transaction record and facilitate record lookup, correction, and deletion.
related_terms: unique award key, transaction, modification

plain_summary: The code Treasury and OMB give each federal account that money flows through, much like a bank account number.
why_it_matters_here: treasury_accounts_funding_this_award lists the accounts that paid for an award, which can help trace which programs fund a cell.
official_definition: The account identification codes assigned by the Department of the Treasury to individual appropriation, receipt, or other fund accounts.
pinpoint: USAspending glossary, term 'Treasury Account Symbol (TAS)', official text
related_terms: federal account, appropriation, File A, GTAS, CGAC

also_called: Unique Entity ID, Unique Entity Identifier, SAM UEI, recipient_uei
plain_summary: The 12-character ID that SAM.gov gives each registered entity. It replaced DUNS in April 2022.
why_it_matters_here: recipient_uei is never blank back to FY2008, because USAspending filled in UEIs for older rows after the switch.
official_definition: Unique entity identifier means a number or other identifier used to identify a specific commercial, nonprofit, or Government entity.
pinpoint: FAR 2.101(b), definition of unique entity identifier
related_terms: DUNS, parent UEI, SAM.gov, CAGE code

also_called: highest-level owner, parent company, parent recipient
plain_summary: The top company in a corporate family, the one that no other entity owns or controls. Grouping by ultimate parent counts a company's subsidiaries as one vendor.
why_it_matters_here: Concentration depends on whether subsidiaries count as one vendor. We use the parent recorded at the time of each action.
official_definition: The recipient_parent data elements reference the ultimate parent of an awardee or recipient and can be used to group together related recipients.
pinpoint: Analyst's Guide, Recipient data elements, p. 17 (PDF p. 17)
related_terms: parent UEI, parent DUNS, vendor, parent test

plain_summary: USAspending's ID for a whole award, built from the PIID, the reporting agency and the parent IDV. It starts with CONT_AWD_ for contracts and orders and CONT_IDV_ for IDVs.
why_it_matters_here: Our award-level checks, such as flags B05, B06 and J03, group rows by this key.
official_definition: Derived unique record key used by the Broker to identify the prime award.
related_terms: PIID, transaction key, award, referenced IDV

plain_summary: An award that appears in agency account data (File C) or in award data (File D1 or D2), but not both, because the two lack a shared award ID.
why_it_matters_here: Unlinked contracts still appear in our files. They lack the account columns that File C supplies.
official_definition: Unlinked awards lack a shared award ID that allows a match between financial system data and award reporting data.
related_terms: File C, File D1, Treasury Account Symbol

plain_summary: Two gold bullion contract vehicles from May 2010 that each record a $10 billion obligation on the vehicle record. The orders placed under them carry their own obligations.
why_it_matters_here: Counting the vehicle rows and the orders may double count. The proposal keeps both rows out of HHI until a source confirms them.
related_terms: IDV, BOA, base and all options value, delivery order

plain_summary: The official public website for federal spending data. It shows contract data copied from FPDS, along with grants and agency account data. Treasury runs it.
why_it_matters_here: All of our data comes from USAspending's Award Data Archive, so its rules for building files shape our data.
official_definition: Since 2007, USAspending.gov has reported information on federal awards (contracts, grants, loans, and other awards) as required by FFATA.
related_terms: Award Data Archive, FFATA, DATA Act, FPDS, File D1, DATA Act Broker

plain_summary: In our measure, the parent UEI on a row, or the recipient UEI where the parent is blank. Rows with both blank form one vendor.
why_it_matters_here: Vendor shares feed HHI and CR4, so the vendor rule decides whether subsidiaries count together.
related_terms: parent UEI, UEI, vendor-cell, ultimate parent
