plain_summary: A vendor's net dollars in a cell divided by the cell's net dollars. In version 2 illustrations, shares use vendors with a positive net only.
why_it_matters_here: HHI and CR4 are built from vendor shares, and shares of a negative cell total have no meaning.
related_terms: vendor-cell, HHI, top-4 share, negative vendor total

plain_summary: One vendor's rows within one cell, summed to a net total.
why_it_matters_here: Vendor-cells are the units whose shares make up HHI. There are 7,847,575 of them.
related_terms: cell, vendor, negative vendor total, net dollars

plain_summary: Checks in which an agency samples its own FPDS records and compares them with the contract files. OMB has required them since 2007. The reviewer must not be the person who awarded the contract.
why_it_matters_here: Agency V&V results are the main government measure of FPDS field accuracy, the fields our measure relies on.
official_definition: Establish an agency-wide requirement for routine, statistically-valid data verification and validation. The verification and validation must be conducted by an organization or person that did not award the contracts being reviewed.
pinpoint: OFPP memorandum of March 9, 2007, p. 1 (PDF p. 1)
related_terms: data quality certification, FPDS, OMB

plain_summary: A small business at least 51% owned and run by women.
why_it_matters_here: WOSB set-asides limit who can bid, which can shape concentration in a cell.
official_definition: That is at least 51 percent owned by one or more women
pinpoint: FAR 2.101(b), definition of women-owned small business concern, paragraph (1)(i)
related_terms: set-aside, small business concern, NAICS

plain_summary: One agency awards and runs a contract for another agency that needs the work. The agency that does the buying is the awarding agency on the record.
why_it_matters_here: Dollars land in the cells of the agency that did the buying, so the agency that paid for the work looks smaller.
official_definition: Assisted acquisition means a type of interagency acquisition where a servicing agency performs acquisition activities on a requesting agency's behalf, such as awarding and administering a contract, task order, or delivery order.
related_terms: interagency acquisition, awarding agency, funding agency

plain_summary: Any purchase where one agency gets goods or services through another agency, either by having it award the contract or by ordering from its contract.
why_it_matters_here: These purchases can put one agency's demand in another agency's cells.
official_definition: Interagency acquisition means a procedure by which an agency needing supplies or services (the requesting agency) obtains them from another agency (the servicing agency), by an assisted acquisition or a direct acquisition.
related_terms: assisted acquisition, multi-agency contract, GWAC

plain_summary: The government ends all or part of a contract because it no longer needs the work, with no fault by the vendor. The ending is recorded as a modification, often with a deobligation.
why_it_matters_here: Terminations in FY2025 add deobligations that can make vendor totals negative.
official_definition: Termination for convenience means the exercise of the Government's right to completely or partially terminate performance of work under a contract when it is in the Government's interest.
related_terms: modification, deobligation, negative vendor total

plain_summary: A contract whose work requires access to classified information. Contract actions whose reported data would be classified are kept out of FPDS.
why_it_matters_here: Classified buying is missing from every year of our data, with no marker in the rows.
official_definition: Classified contract means any contract in which the contractor or its employees must have access to classified information during contract performance.
related_terms: FAR subpart 4.6, contract action

plain_summary: Permission for an agency to depart from the FAR. A class deviation covers a whole group of contract actions, and agencies use them to adopt new rules early.
why_it_matters_here: Agencies adopted the $10,000 micro-purchase threshold and the 2025 FAR rewrite by class deviation on different dates, so a rule change reaches agencies at different times.
official_definition: Deviation means any one or combination of the following: (a) The issuance or use of a policy, procedure, solicitation provision (see definition in 2.101), contract clause (see definition in 2.101), method, or practice of conducting acquisition actions of any kind at any stage of the acquisition process that is inconsistent with the FAR.
related_terms: FAR, micro-purchase threshold, Revolutionary FAR Overhaul

plain_summary: A contract under which a firm runs a government-owned laboratory or plant for an agency, mostly at the Department of Energy. The operator buys from many subcontractors who do not appear in FPDS.
why_it_matters_here: Each operator shows up as one very large vendor, so Department of Energy cells look highly concentrated.
official_definition: Management and operating contract means an agreement under which the Government contracts for the operation, maintenance, or support, on its behalf, of a Government-owned or -controlled research, development, special production, or testing establishment wholly or principally devoted to one or more major programs of the contracting Federal agency.
related_terms: vendor, sub-award, HHI

plain_summary: A small cash fund an agency keeps for minor purchases paid in cash. Purchases from it below the micro-purchase threshold are not reported to FPDS.
why_it_matters_here: This spending is outside our data by rule.
official_definition: Imprest fund means a cash fund of a fixed amount established by an advance of funds, without charge to an appropriation, from an agency finance or disbursing officer to a duly appointed cashier, for disbursement as needed from time to time in making payment in cash for relatively small amounts.
related_terms: micro-purchase, government purchase card, FAR subpart 4.6

plain_summary: A federal program that buys certain supplies and services from nonprofit agencies that employ people who are blind or have severe disabilities. Purchases at its stores are not reported to FPDS.
why_it_matters_here: GSA already reports the stocked items, so the buying agencies' cells look smaller than their real demand.
pinpoint: FAR 8.701, definitions of central nonprofit agency and ordering office
related_terms: GSA, FAR subpart 4.6

plain_summary: An exception that lets an agency limit competition when waiting would seriously harm the government. Such awards may be reported to FPDS up to 30 days late.
why_it_matters_here: GAO found this exception miscoded in 28 of 62 sampled contracts, so the recorded reason for limited competition is unreliable.
official_definition: When the agency's need for the supplies or services is of such an unusual and compelling urgency that the Government would be seriously injured unless the agency is permitted to limit the number of sources from which it solicits bids or proposals, full and open competition need not be provided for.
related_terms: other than full and open competition, full and open competition, not competed

also_called: Federal Acquisition Regulatory Council, DAR Council, CAA Council
plain_summary: The group that writes and revises the FAR. It works through two councils, one for defense agencies and one for civilian agencies.
why_it_matters_here: Its rule changes, published in the Federal Register, set what agencies must report to FPDS in each year of our data.
official_definition: Subject to the authorities discussed in 1.103, revisions to the FAR will be prepared and issued through the coordinated action of two councils, the Defense Acquisition Regulations Council (DAR Council) and the Civilian Agency Acquisition Council (CAA Council).
related_terms: FAR, Federal Acquisition Circular, Federal Register

plain_summary: One FPDS record that sums many contract actions, filed at least monthly. Its number of actions field holds the count.
why_it_matters_here: Row counts understate the real number of actions wherever express reports are used.
official_definition: Express reporting (consolidated reporting of multiple contract actions, to be submitted at least monthly).
related_terms: contract action report, FPDS, generic entity identifier

plain_summary: DoD's companion to the DFARS. It holds procedures and guidance that sit beside the binding rules, including DoD's instructions for reporting to FPDS.
why_it_matters_here: The written basis for DoD's 90-day delay is PGI 204.604(2), first seen in its 2016 revision.
related_terms: DFARS, DoD 90-day delay, FAR

plain_summary: A rewrite of the FAR that began in 2025 to shorten it and move its rules into a new structure. The contract reporting rules of FAR subpart 4.6 become section 4.301.
why_it_matters_here: FY2025 rows were reported under the old rules, so the rewrite matters for later releases.
related_terms: FAR, FAR subpart 4.6, deviation

plain_summary: Part of a federal award that the main recipient passes to another firm or group to carry out. Sub-awards are reported apart from the main awards and are outside our data.
why_it_matters_here: Money a vendor passes to its subcontractors stays with that vendor in our shares.
official_definition: An award provided by a pass-through entity to a subrecipient for the subrecipient to carry out part of a federal award received by the pass-through entity.
related_terms: award, File F, management and operating contract

plain_summary: Federal money given to support a public purpose, such as grants, loans and direct payments. It is reported apart from contracts and is outside our data.
why_it_matters_here: Several audits mix assistance awards with contracts, so their error rates do not describe contract rows alone.
official_definition: A federal program, service, or activity that directly aids organizations, individuals, or state/local/tribal governments.
pinpoint: USAspending glossary, Financial Assistance, plain text
related_terms: File D2, award, contract action

plain_summary: A firm that manages a group of companies that win other transaction agreements together. FPDS often names the manager as the vendor, even though member firms do the work.
why_it_matters_here: A manager counted as the vendor makes a cell look more concentrated than it is.
official_definition: The CMO is a single point of contact for the government, managing hundreds of consortium members and providing administrative services to both the government and vendors.
related_terms: other transaction agreement, vendor, top-4 share

plain_summary: The family of GSA systems for federal award data, including SAM.gov and FPDS. GSA paused its modernization in September 2023 for lack of funds.
why_it_matters_here: Fixes to FPDS fields such as the product code are unlikely while the systems are frozen.
official_definition: FPDS is part of the Integrated Award Environment (IAE), a suite of systems administered by the General Services Administration (GSA) that tracks federal award data.
related_terms: FPDS, SAM.gov, GSA
